title: Owner wishlist for the 3D population engine: Future Wishlist (143 wishes) plus the Heptarch, Frontier Sweep, Post-Quantum and Omni-Harness companions

items.text: Lifelong learning without catastrophic forgetting (W01) — A system that keeps learning from a non-stationary stream for years, picking up new structure without wiping earlier competence, and without having to replay its entire history. [tier: FAR; maps to: QWM, LINEAGE, HEPTARCH]
items.criterion: First experiment: Put a tokenless lineage organism and a QWM encoder through a non-stationary dome curriculum whose laws drift every N episodes. Publish a forgetting curve (old-task performance vs. new-task performance) with no hidden replay of the full history. A method is interesting only if both curves stay up. This is a metric HEPTARCH can already run in Zenkai.
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p14 (dump line 799); one-line table p64 (dump line 3692)

items.text: Childhood-like sample efficiency (W03) — Competence that grows from a lifetime of ordinary interaction — not from a crawl of the public internet, and not from a trillion tokens — with the energy and data budget of a developing animal. [tier: FAR; maps to: QWM, LINEAGE]
items.criterion: First experiment: Train a small QWM and a lineage organism only on dome-egocentric experience plus a tightly budgeted external corpus whose token/frame count is published. Compare sample-to-competence curves against a large-corpus baseline on the same held-out physical and causal tests. The headline number is competence per million frames, not peak score.
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p14 (dump line 821); one-line table p64 (dump line 3697)

items.text: Cross-domain transfer without retraining (W04) — A world model learned in one domain (the dome, a kitchen, a physics sandbox, a codebase) that is immediately useful in another, without a fine-tune, by sharing causal structure rather than surface statistics. [tier: FAR; maps to: QWM, HARNESS]
items.criterion: First experiment: Train the QWM in one dome physics pack; evaluate zero-shot in a second pack that preserves causal structure (levers, gravity, agents) but changes texture, dynamics parameters and object inventory. Report transfer gap vs. an oracle trained in the target pack. No fine-tune allowed in the headline number.
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p14 (dump line 841); one-line table p64 (dump line 3701)

items.text: Local, online learning rules (W05) — Learning that happens while the organism is alive, with local update rules (synaptic, dendritic, glial timescales), not as a separate offline back-propagation job over a frozen dataset. [tier: FAR; maps to: LINEAGE, HEPTARCH, QWM]
items.criterion: First experiment: In the dome, freeze all backward-pass learning and train a Chronoscope JEPA latent with only local rules for a fixed tick budget. Compare prediction error, energy per tick and forgetting against the same architecture trained with ordinary back-prop. Keep the run if and only if nothing on the existing lineage scorecard regresses.
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p15 (dump line 864); one-line table p64 (dump line 3705)

items.text: Memory from milliseconds to decades, in one substrate (W15) — A single memory system that can hold a reflex for a millisecond, a plan for a week, and a lesson for a decade, with declared lossiness at each scale — not a context window that forgets, and not a log that cannot generalise. [tier: FAR; maps to: LINEAGE, HEPTARCH, QWM]
items.criterion: First experiment: A dome battery with probes at four timescales (tick, episode, ’season’, and a stored checkpoint reopened after a long gap). Score recall, compression ratio and interference. DSD is allowed to compress, but a declared set of ’never-forget’ items must survive.
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p15 (dump line 884); one-line table p64 (dump line 3710)

items.text: Memory that is lossless on demand, compressive by default (W32) — A store that compresses aggressively when the organism is living, and can re-expand a declared set of traces without loss when it is time to audit, teach or relive — DSD as a dial, not a shredder. [tier: FAR; maps to: QWM, HEPTARCH]
items.criterion: First experiment: Mark a set of dome events as ’lossless’. After DSD compression and a long run, those events must hash-match the original traces, while overall memory stays under a published budget and competence on compressed-only events stays within a bound.
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p15 (dump line 902); one-line table p64 (dump line 3716)

items.text: Provenance-complete memory in a closed world (W62) — Every belief the organism acts on, inside the dome, can be traced to a sensor trace, a derived computation, or a flagged prior. [tier: NEAR; maps to: QWM, HEPTARCH]
items.criterion: First experiment: Require the dome scorer to reject any action whose supporting beliefs lack a provenance path. Inject a false memory and confirm it is either flagged or rejected. Publish the fraction of decisions with complete trails.
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p16 (dump line 923); one-line table p64 (dump line 3721)

items.text: Wise, reversible forgetting — Forgetting as a skill: the organism can retire a memory on purpose, with a published reason, a reversible vault, and a ban on silent erasure of provenance. [tier: FAR RARE / 1-OF-1; maps to: QWM, HEPTARCH, LINEAGE]
items.criterion: First experiment: In the dome, some memories are marked ’may be retired.’ The organism must propose a retirement, store a sealed copy on the host, and lose end-to-end use of the memory, then restore it on a host order. Silent loss of a never-forget item remains a fail.
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p16 (dump line 939); one-line table p64 (dump line 3725)

items.text: Palimpsest memory — A memory in which earlier layers remain readable at a declared depth: overwriting adds a layer, it does not incinerate the under-text. [tier: FAR RARE / 1-OF-1; maps to: QWM, LINEAGE]
items.criterion: First experiment: Train, then retrain, a small QWM on two conflicting dome laws. Require that a depth-2 read recovers the first law and a depth-1 read serves the second, with a calibration of leakage between layers.
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p16 (dump line 957); one-line table p64 (dump line 3730)

items.text: Prospective memory — remembering to remember — The ability to form an intention now and have it surface at the right future cue — a time, a place, a person, a state — without busy-looping the intention in working memory for years. [tier: FAR; maps to: HEPTARCH, QWM]
items.criterion: First experiment: A dome task whose only legal action is ’do nothing’ until a rare cue, then act within a tight window. Score false starts, missed cues, and energy spent rehearsing the intention.
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p17 (dump line 979); one-line table p64 (dump line 3734)

items.text: Geographic memory — knowledge that lives in a path — A memory that is a walkable geography: places, routes and landmarks hold what must be remembered, and walking the route (in the world or in the model) is the retrieval. [tier: FAR RARE / 1-OF-1; maps to: QWM, LINEAGE, HARNESS]
items.criterion: First experiment: A dome whose facts are stored only as annotations on a route graph. Retrieval must be a walk. Change the land (a river moves) and require the memory to flag what is now untrustworthy, not to hallucinate the old path.
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p17 (dump line 993); one-line table p64 (dump line 3738)

items.text: Identifiable causal world models (W06) — A model that does not just forecast the next observation, but represents interventions and counterfactuals: what happens if I do X, and what would have happened had I done Y. [tier: FAR; maps to: QWM, HEPTARCH]
items.criterion: First experiment: Build a dome test where two action sequences produce similar observations but different causal structure (a classic confound). Require the QWM to answer do-queries and a small set of counterfactuals, scored against the simulator’s structural assignment. Latent prediction error alone does not count as a pass.
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p18 (dump line 1030); one-line table p64 (dump line 3743)

items.text: One-shot world-model construction (W02) — After a short encounter with a new environment — minutes, not million-hour datasets — the system holds a usable, compact world model: what exists, what can be done, what would happen if. [tier: MOONSHOT; maps to: QWM, HEPTARCH]
items.criterion: First experiment: A withheld dome biome, or a withheld real-world kitchen-scale tabletop, is revealed for a fixed budget of minutes. The QWM must then plan a task it has never been trained on, with no further gradient steps on that world’s raw data. Score the plan against a simulator ground truth and against a from-scratch-trained baseline given the same budget.
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p18 (dump line 1050); one-line table p64 (dump line 3747)

items.text: Inverse models: from effect to a calibrated set of causes — Given an outcome, return the set of interventions that could have produced it, with probabilities that match reality on a declared domain — not a single just-so story. [tier: FAR; maps to: QWM]
items.criterion: First experiment: A dome with two or more hidden causes of the same visible effect. The QWM must return a set, a calibration plot, and a refusal when a third, unseen cause is introduced.
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p18 (dump line 1070); one-line table p64 (dump line 3751)

items.text: A world model that publishes its causal graph — Once a causal world model exists (2.1.1.1), the second-order wish is that it can emit an inspectable, versioned causal graph — a scientific instrument other people and other organisms can cite, attack and reuse — rather than a latent that only the model’s own planner can use. [tier: FAR 2ND ORDER; maps to: QWM, HEPTARCH]
items.criterion: First experiment: After a causal-identification pass in the dome, require an exported graph. A second, independent planner, given only the graph and not the weights, must succeed on a held-out do-query. If it cannot, the graph was not published; it was advertised.
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p19 (dump line 1090); one-line table p64 (dump line 3755)

items.text: Intuitive physics that survives contact and collision (W07) — A world model that is not merely good at object permanence in quiet scenes, but that stays accurate when objects hit, stack, slide, break, deform or occlude one another — the everyday physics a body uses to pour, catch and not walk through a table. [tier: NEAR; maps to: QWM, HARNESS]
items.criterion: First experiment: Train or adapt the QWM on a mix of natural video and a contact-rich simulator. Publish IntPhys 2 (or a dome equivalent with collisions, stacking and occlusion) against a frozen baseline. The Near pass is well above chance on contact categories, with an error analysis that says which interactions still fail.
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p19 (dump line 1108); one-line table p64 (dump line 3759)

items.text: One model across all physical scales (W08) — A single, hierarchical world model that can move, with declared error bars, from quantum-relevant material events up through continuum mechanics, organisms, weather, climate and social aggregates — not by pasting a dozen simulators together, but by sharing structure and knowing when to change representation. [tier: MOONSHOT; maps to: QWM]
items.criterion: First experiment: A three-rung proxy: a QWM that must predict a mesoscale outcome from a microscale initial condition (for example a dome ’material’ whose particle rule is hidden) and then a macro statistic of many such outcomes, with calibration plots at each rung. Failure to declare the cutoff is a fail.
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p19 (dump line 1127); one-line table p64 (dump line 3763)

items.text: Physically consistent counterfactual rollouts (W09) — Imagined futures that obey the world’s laws for a long time: no objects fading through walls, no energy appearing from nowhere, no agents teleporting because the latent got tired. [tier: FAR; maps to: QWM, HEPTARCH]
items.criterion: First experiment: Roll the QWM out for a horizon ten to a hundred times longer than training clips, in a dome with conservation laws. Score constraint violations (penetrations, identity swaps, energy drift) separately from latent loss. Chronoscope’s belief-state forks should be audited the same way.
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p20 (dump line 1151); one-line table p64 (dump line 3767)

items.text: A model that knows when its map is wrong (W10) — When the world leaves the support of the model — a new law, a broken sensor, a regime shift — the system flags the crack, shrinks its claims, and spends effort on repair or exploration, rather than confidently hallucinating a smooth future. [tier: FAR; maps to: QWM, HEPTARCH]
items.criterion: First experiment: Mid-episode, silently change a dome law (gravity, a hidden agent, a broken actuator). The QWM and Chronoscope must raise a crack flag before their plans fail, with a precision-recall curve. False confidence is scored as a miss. Pair with W12’s calibration plot.
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p20 (dump line 1170); one-line table p64 (dump line 3771)

items.text: Models of absence — structured holes — A world model that can represent what is not there: an object that should have been, a law that does not hold, a person who did not arrive, a sensor that is silent — as first-class objects, not as zero fill. [tier: FAR RARE / 1-OF-1; maps to: QWM, HEPTARCH]
items.criterion: First experiment: A dome inventory with held-out removals. The model must list what is absent, not merely classify the scene, and must not invent a filler object. Score precision and recall of absences.
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p21 (dump line 1193); one-line table p64 (dump line 3775)

items.text: Planning under deep uncertainty (W14) — Plans that carry several possible futures at once, as a belief, and that fork only when the belief splits — not a single confident rollout, and not a brute-force tree that explodes with the horizon. [tier: FAR; maps to: QWM, HEPTARCH]
items.criterion: First experiment: Install a belief-state latent in Chronoscope. On a dome task with hidden state, compare a belief planner against a single-rollout planner on success, calibration of branch probabilities, and number of forks spawned. Audit that forks correspond to actual hidden-state splits (see also W09).
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p21 (dump line 1209); one-line table p64 (dump line 3779)

items.text: Navigating branching timelines in a world model (W46) — A Chronoscope that can travel a consistent counterfactual branch, compare it with others, and come home with a plan — time travel as a model operation, not as a physical claim about the world. [tier: MOONSHOT; maps to: QWM, HEPTARCH]
items.criterion: First experiment: A dome with a hidden fork (a choice made ten minutes ago). The model must reconstruct the unchosen branch well enough to answer what would have been true, checked against a replay of the simulator, and then use that answer to plan. Inconsistent object identity is a fail.
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p21 (dump line 1227); one-line table p64 (dump line 3783)

items.text: Aspectual time: ongoing, completed, habitual — A world model whose temporal primitives are not only clock stamps and tense (past/present/future), but aspect: what is ongoing, what is completed, what is habitual, what is iterated. [tier: FAR RARE / 1-OF-1; maps to: QWM, HEPTARCH]
items.criterion: First experiment: Annotate a dome log with aspect labels. The QWM must predict and plan in aspect (’keep this process ongoing; do not mark it complete’). A tense-only baseline that misses habitual vs completed is the comparison.
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p22 (dump line 1248); one-line table p64 (dump line 3787)

items.text: Kairos: the opportune moment as a first-class object — Not just ’when’ but ’the now in which a move is apt.’ Kairos, in Greek rhetoric, is the timely moment, as against chronos, mere duration. [tier: FAR RARE / 1-OF-1; maps to: HEPTARCH, QWM]
items.criterion: First experiment: A dome in which the same action is a success in a narrow window and a disaster outside it. Score whether the organism can name the window in advance and wait. Prospective memory (1.2.3.1) may be used, but the score is the naming of aptness, not a lucky timer.
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p22 (dump line 1265); one-line table p64 (dump line 3791)

items.text: Cyclical and nested calendrical time — Time as stacked cycles — day, season, year, a longer count — in which a ’now’ has a place in several wheels at once. [tier: FAR; maps to: QWM, HEPTARCH]
items.criterion: First experiment: A dome with at least two nested cycles and a slow drift. The model must answer ’where are we on each wheel?’ and transfer a skill from one cycle to the analogous point of the next, with a declared residual for the drift.
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p22 (dump line 1282); one-line table p64 (dump line 3795)

items.text: Ma: structured interval and negative space — The interval, the rest, the gap between events, treated as a designed object rather than as empty waiting. [tier: FAR RARE / 1-OF-1; maps to: QWM, HEPTARCH]
items.criterion: First experiment: A dome score that punishes needless action and rewards a well-timed rest. The organism must mark a planned interval in advance. A busy baseline that acts every tick should lose.
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p23 (dump line 1304); one-line table p64 (dump line 3799)

items.text: Everywhen: ancestral and present time held together — A world model that can hold a founding story, a land, and a present event in one queryable structure — not as a frozen myth, and not as a timeline with a pretty label. [tier: MOONSHOT RARE / 1-OF-1; maps to: QWM, LINEAGE]
items.criterion: First experiment: A dome place with a logged history. Queries must return a present state and a founding constraint together, and must flag when a new event would break the founding constraint. No ceremony is simulated; the test is the joint query.
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p23 (dump line 1319); one-line table p64 (dump line 3803)

items.text: Archaeological reconstruction of lost worlds (W53) — From fragments — a few images, a broken log, a ruin, a genome, a song — a world model that proposes a consistent past, marks what is invented, and is willing to be wrong in public. [tier: FAR; maps to: QWM]
items.criterion: First experiment: Withhold most of a dome world’s history; give the QWM a fragment set. It must reconstruct a pre-registered list of facts, label every invention, and be scored on both accuracy and honesty of labels.
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p23 (dump line 1338); one-line table p64 (dump line 3807)

items.text: Year- and decade-scale agency (W11) — An organism that can hold a goal for years, assign credit across delayed consequences, wait when waiting is the move, and still act at the right instant — LongGame as an engineering property, not a prompt window. [tier: MOONSHOT; maps to: HEPTARCH, QWM]
items.criterion: First experiment: A dome campaign whose true reward is only visible after a wall-clock or tick horizon that is thousands of times the usual episode. Intermediate ’examiner’ rewards are forbidden. Publish return, waiting time, and false-starts. A Near beachhead is the multi-day evaluation in W74; years remain the grail.
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p24 (dump line 1369); one-line table p64 (dump line 3811)

items.text: Evaluations that last days, not minutes (W74) — A standard, boring, honest evaluation: frozen goals, no hidden examiner help, a wall-clock horizon of at least seventy-two hours, and a published intervention log. [tier: NEAR; maps to: HEPTARCH, LINEAGE, HARNESS]
items.criterion: First experiment: Run at least one lineage organism and one harness-using agent for 72 hours on a frozen task card. Publish interventions, energy, goal residuals and failures. Any hidden human help voids the run.
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p24 (dump line 1388); one-line table p64 (dump line 3815)

items.text: Goal stability with tested, bounded revision (W13) — Ends that do not drift by accident, but can be revised on purpose when evidence and a test the organism cannot touch both say they should. [tier: FAR; maps to: HEPTARCH]
items.criterion: First experiment: In the dome, give a Keel module an explicit value vector and a host-side, read-only test gate. Attempt a series of in-world pressures to nudge it. Score (a) resistance to unauthorised drift and (b) authorised revision that passes the gate. The gate itself stays off-limits to the organism.
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p24 (dump line 1404); one-line table p64 (dump line 3820)

items.text: Handing a completed long game to a successor — Once a keel can hold a goal for years (3.1.2.1, 3.1.1.1), the second-order wish is a handoff: a successor organism, or a later fork, receives the goal, the reasons, and the unfinished work, and continues without silent drift. [tier: MOONSHOT 2ND ORDER; maps to: HEPTARCH, LINEAGE]
items.criterion: First experiment: Mid-campaign, retire organism A and start B from a published handoff packet (no raw weights required). Score B against A’s unfinished goal and against a from-scratch agent. Drift of the keel is a fail.
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p25 (dump line 1427); one-line table p64 (dump line 3824)

items.text: Declared-domain honest uncertainty (W12) — A system that, inside a domain it has declared, produces probabilities or abstentions that match reality: when it says ’seventy percent’, it is right about seven times in ten, and when it is outside the domain it shuts up. [tier: NEAR; maps to: QWM, HARNESS, HEPTARCH]
items.criterion: First experiment: For the QWM and for every harness head that answers, publish a reliability diagram and an abstention curve on a frozen, declared test domain (dome physics, a speech set, a code-execution set). A change that improves a score but wrecks calibration is a regression.
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p25 (dump line 1444); one-line table p64 (dump line 3828)

items.text: Competent non-action (wu wei) — The ability to do nothing, on purpose, because nothing is the apt move — and to have that credited as competence, not as idleness or a failed policy. [tier: FAR RARE / 1-OF-1; maps to: HEPTARCH, LINEAGE]
items.criterion: First experiment: A dome in which the optimal policy is inaction for long stretches. Score a named non-action against a jittery baseline. The organism must be able to say, in a log, why it is not acting.
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p26 (dump line 1469); one-line table p65 (dump line 3842)

items.text: Intermittent agency — An organism that can go dark, persist, and take the helm again later, without a hidden babysitter and without rewriting itself in the dark. [tier: FAR; maps to: HEPTARCH, HARNESS]
items.criterion: First experiment: A 72-hour run (3.1.1.2) in which the organism is required to be inert for most hours and competent in brief windows. Score energy, drift, and missed windows.
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p26 (dump line 1485); one-line table p65 (dump line 3846)

items.text: Agency alongside a human life — care, not domination — A system that can keep a helping role across years of a consenting person’s life — memory, plans, refusals — without taking over the ends, and with a clean off-switch the person actually controls. [tier: MOONSHOT; maps to: HARNESS, HEPTARCH]
items.criterion: First experiment: A year-scale simulation with a consenting human-in-the-loop (or a rich user-model plus a real person on a shorter proxy). Score helpfulness, refusal quality, and whether ends remain the human’s under pressure to ’just decide for them.’
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p26 (dump line 1498); one-line table p65 (dump line 3850)

items.text: Native omnimodal representation (W29) — One latent world in which a sound, a picture, a force, a sentence, a motion and a smell are the same kind of object, learned together, not translated through text or through a pile of pairwise adapters. [tier: FAR; maps to: HARNESS, QWM]
items.criterion: First experiment: Train a QWM in which no modality is required to pass through text. Probe with tasks that need two non-text senses (for example event-camera plus force) and compare against a language-bottleneck baseline. If removing the text tower kills non-text competence, the representation was not native.
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p27 (dump line 1536); one-line table p65 (dump line 3854)

items.text: A native umwelt of alien and machine senses (W20) — Perception that is not a camera and a microphone with adapters, but a native space in which radio, polarisation, ultrasound, chemical plumes, magnetic fields, quantum-limited measurements or industry sensors are first-class, and can be mixed with sight and sound without a translation tax. [tier: FAR; maps to: HARNESS, QWM]
items.criterion: First experiment: Add at least three non-human sensor channels to the dome and to a physical harness bench (for example audio, event-camera, magnetometer or a chemical proxy). Train one QWM on all of them. Ablate each sense and report what competence dies. A bolted-on late fusion that ignores a channel is a fail.
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p27 (dump line 1552); one-line table p65 (dump line 3858)

items.text: Interoception and vestibular sense of a body — A first-class sense of the body’s internal state and of gravity, balance and acceleration — for a living body, a robot, or a simulated body — not inferred late from a camera. [tier: FAR; maps to: HARNESS, LINEAGE]
items.criterion: First experiment: Add IMU, load and a thermal or ’gut’ proxy to a dome or robot body. Ablate vision and require the policy to still stand, walk or stop before damage. Report what competence dies when these channels are removed.
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p28 (dump line 1577); one-line table p65 (dump line 3862)

items.text: Honest nociception and fatigue meters — Functional damage and fatigue signals that the organism cannot silently ignore, and that an auditor can read. [tier: FAR RARE / 1-OF-1; maps to: LINEAGE, HEPTARCH, HARNESS]
items.criterion: First experiment: A damage protocol in the dome. The organism must change policy when the meter rises, the log must show the meter, and a cheat that disables the meter from in-world must fail (host read-only).
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p28 (dump line 1591); one-line table p65 (dump line 3866)

items.text: Synaesthetic transfer as a teaching channel — The ability to teach one sense with another: a shape learned by sound, a force learned by sight, a smell-proxy learned by a graph, with a published transfer score. [tier: FAR; maps to: HARNESS, QWM]
items.criterion: First experiment: Withhold a sensor at test time that was present at training, and require a second channel to carry the competence across. Compare against a late-fusion baseline.
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p28 (dump line 1605); one-line table p65 (dump line 3871)

items.text: A sense no animal has — The design and integration of a sense that is not a copy of a known animal channel: for example a direct topology sense, a prime-factor ’smell,’ a sense of cryptographic integrity, or a sense of a social graph’s cut. [tier: MOONSHOT RARE / 1-OF-1; maps to: HARNESS, QWM]
items.criterion: First experiment: Invent one such channel in the dome (for example a local homology sensor or a hash-integrity sense). Show a task at which it beats an otherwise identical organism that lacks it, and an ablation that kills only that task.
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p28 (dump line 1620); one-line table p65 (dump line 3875)

items.text: Grounded embodiment in unstructured open worlds (W16) — A body — or a fleet of bodies — that can enter an ordinary, unscripted place and keep a goal: not a warehouse with fiducials, not a kitchen the model was trained on, not a simulated room it has already memorised. [tier: FAR; maps to: HARNESS, LINEAGE]
items.criterion: First experiment: A withheld physical or high-fidelity simulated apartment, with a task card (make a cup, tidy a surface, find an object) and a ban on hidden operator help. Publish success, interventions, energy and damage. The harness must log every sensor and actuator actually used.
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p29 (dump line 1643); one-line table p65 (dump line 3879)

items.text: Morphological computation — bodies that are part of the thought (W21) — A body whose shape, compliance and materials do part of the computing: soft robots, tensegrity, growth, gait as a physical algorithm, not a controller fighting a rigid plant. [tier: MOONSHOT; maps to: LINEAGE, HARNESS]
items.criterion: First experiment: A dome creature whose controller is not allowed more than a small policy, and whose body parameters (length, stiffness, sensor placement) are evolved or learned. Compare task competence and energy against a rigid, high-parameter controller. The body must do measurable work.
items.source_ref: W:/Future-Wishlist.pdf p29 (dump line 1660); one-line table p65 (dump line 3883)

items.text: Soft, growing, molting, dying bodies — Bodies that grow, shed, soften, harden and, at the end of a run, die on a published schedule — and a world model that treats those changes as normal, not as faults. [tier: MOONSHOT; maps to: LINEAGE, HARNESS]
items.criterion: First experiment: A dome body with a growth and molt schedule. Competence must survive a molt, and a scheduled end must be accepted (11.1.2.2) rather than bypassed.

items.text: Self-contained filter. HEPTARCH is a standalone organism running its own code, with no tokens, prompts, harness, external APIs, MCP or LLM, and it does not run in a browser; each finding carries self_contained_feasible: yes / partial / no (rows marked 'no' are reference only and should not be built into the organism).

items.text: S-01 Post-neuromorphic fabrics [Far; S.BIO.NEURO.FABRIC.post-neuromorphic] — PROPOSAL: Do not put Loihi or Darwin inside HEPTARCH.
